message.content: {"passages":[{"reference":"7.1","text":"On the fourth day of our stay in Tyre, toward dawn, when Peter had come forward, not a few inhabitants of the neighboring places and very many from Tyre itself met him and cried out, saying, “May God have mercy on us through you; may he heal us through you.” Peter stood on a certain high stone so that he could be seen by everyone and, after greeting them in accordance with the law that reveres God, began as follows:","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"τῆς ἐν Τύρῳ ἡμῶν ἐπιδημίας","chosen":"of our stay in Tyre","rationale":"Here ἐπιδημία denotes a temporary residence or stay, not an epidemic or an official visitation."},{"source_quote":"ὑπὸ τὸν ὄρθρον","chosen":"toward dawn","rationale":"The phrase locates the event near the approach of daybreak."},{"source_quote":"προεληλυθότι τῷ Πέτρῳ","chosen":"when Peter had come forward","rationale":"The perfect participle presents Peter as having gone out or come forward; “come forward” fits his subsequent public address without specifying an unmentioned building."},{"source_quote":"προσαγορεύσας θεοσεβεῖ νόμῳ","chosen":"after greeting them in accordance with the law that reveres God","rationale":"προσαγορεύω means greet or address, while the dative θεοσεβεῖ νόμῳ expresses the God-revering rule or manner governing the greeting; “with a God-revering greeting” is also possible."}],"source_issues":[]},{"reference":"7.2","text":"God, who created heaven and the universe, lacks no means for the salvation of those who wish to be saved. Therefore, no one, through rashness, should accuse him of lacking benevolence toward humanity on account of things that appear bad. For the outcomes of what happens to a human being are unknown to humans and are suspected of tending toward evil, but they are known to God as things that will turn out well. Take Simon as an immediate example: being God’s left-hand power and holding authority over those who do not know God for the purpose of doing harm, he was able to surround you with diseases. These diseases, having been permitted to arise through God’s good providence, compelled you, after you had looked around for and found the one able to heal, to accept, on the pretext of treatment of the body, the things that seem good to God and to be persuaded to set your minds on them, so that in this way, together with your bodies that are to be saved, you might also have your souls safe.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"οὐ λείπει πρόφασις πρὸς σωτηρίαν","chosen":"lacks no means for the salvation","rationale":"Although πρόφασις can mean “pretext,” here it denotes an occasion, resource, or means directed toward salvation."},{"source_quote":"ὡς μὴ φιλάνθρωπον","chosen":"of lacking benevolence toward humanity","rationale":"φιλάνθρωπος describes one who is humane or benevolent toward people; the rendering preserves the negation without importing a specialized theological title."},{"source_quote":"αὐτίκα γοῦν Σίμων ἀριστερὰ τοῦ θεοῦ δύναμις ὢν","chosen":"Take Simon as an immediate example: being God’s left-hand power","rationale":"αὐτίκα γοῦν introduces a concrete immediate example, and ἀριστερὰ τοῦ θεοῦ δύναμις directly identifies Simon as the left-hand power of God."},{"source_quote":"τῶν τὸν θεὸν οὐκ εἰδότων ἐπὶ κακοποιΐᾳ τὴν ἐξουσίαν ἔχων","chosen":"holding authority over those who do not know God for the purpose of doing harm","rationale":"The genitive marks those over whom the authority operates, while ἐπὶ κακοποιΐᾳ states its harmful purpose or function."},{"source_quote":"τὰ θεῷ δοκοῦντα ἀναδεξαμένους πεισθῆναι φρονεῖν","chosen":"to accept the things that seem good to God and to be persuaded to set your minds on them","rationale":"The participle describes accepting what is pleasing to God, followed by persuasion in thought. More literally, the final words can be rendered “to be persuaded to think,” but English benefits from making the contextually supplied object explicit."}],"source_issues":[]},{"reference":"7.3","text":"I learn, then, that after sacrificing an ox he gave you a feast in the middle of the marketplace, and that in this way, carried away by much wine, you joined the evil demons in showing hospitality to their ruler. Thus most of you were seized by afflictions, because in ignorance you drew against yourselves, with your own hands, the sword of destruction. For the demons would not have had authority against you if you had not first shared a meal with their ruler. From the beginning, God, who created everything, laid down this law for the two rulers in every instance—the ruler of the right and the ruler of the left: neither of them is to have authority unless he first becomes the table companion of someone whom he wishes to benefit or harm. As, then, by partaking of the sacrifices dedicated to demons you were enslaved to the leader of evil, so, if you cease from these things and take refuge in God through the good, right-hand leader, honoring him without sacrifice by doing what he wishes, know well that along with the healing of the body you will also have healthy souls. For he alone, destroying through the left hand, can give life through the right hand; likewise, he can both strike and raise up one who lies fallen.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"ὡς βουθυτήσας εἱστίασεν ὑμᾶς","chosen":"that after sacrificing an ox he gave you a feast","rationale":"βουθυτέω denotes sacrificing an ox or cattle. The unexpressed subject is most naturally Simon from the preceding context."},{"source_quote":"ἅμα τοῖς πονηροῖς δαίμοσιν τὸν ἄρχοντα αὐτῶν ἐφιλοφρονεῖσθε","chosen":"you joined the evil demons in showing hospitality to their ruler","rationale":"φιλοφρονέομαι can mean welcome, entertain, or treat graciously. “Showing hospitality” preserves the banquet setting, though “paying court to” is also possible."},{"source_quote":"ὁμοδίαιτοι ἐγεγόνειτε","chosen":"you had first shared a meal","rationale":"ὁμοδίαιτος can describe living or dining together. The surrounding references to sacrifices and table fellowship support the meal-related rendering."},{"source_quote":"δυσὶν ἑκάστοτε ἄρχουσι, δεξιῶν τε καὶ εὐωνύμων","chosen":"for the two rulers in every instance—the ruler of the right and the ruler of the left","rationale":"ἑκάστοτε indicates each recurring instance, while the genitives distinguish the right-hand and left-hand sides or powers. “For each pair of rulers, of right and left” is a viable alternative."},{"source_quote":"ἀθύτοις τιμαῖς ποιοῦντες ἃ βούλεται","chosen":"honoring him without sacrifice by doing what he wishes","rationale":"ἀθύτοις describes honors not involving sacrifice. The rendering takes doing what God wishes as the form of those non-sacrificial honors."},{"source_quote":"αὐτὸς γὰρ μόνος διὰ τῆς ἀριστερᾶς ἀναιρῶν διὰ τῆς δεξιᾶς ζωοποιῆσαι δύναται","chosen":"For he alone, destroying through the left hand, can give life through the right hand","rationale":"The participle ἀναιρῶν describes destruction through the left, while the infinitive ζωοποιῆσαι with δύναται states his ability to give life through the right."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"·ἀθύτοις τιμαῖς","issue":"An isolated raised point is printed immediately before ἀθύτοις despite the preceding comma. It appears to be stray or redundant punctuation and contributes no lexical content.","proposed_reading":"ἀθύτοις τιμαῖς","blocks_publication":false}]},{"reference":"7.4","text":"For this reason, after first being deceived by Simon the forerunner, you died to God in your souls, and your bodies were struck. But in the same way you can, a second time, through reorientation—as I said—accept the things pleasing to God and both restore your bodies to health and recover your souls. What pleases God is this: to pray to him; to make requests of him as the one who gives everything according to a judicial law; to abstain from “the table of demons”; not to taste dead flesh; not to touch blood; and to wash oneself clean of every pollution. As for the rest, hear it, all of you, in one saying, just as the Jews who revere God have heard it, taking up one mind in many bodies: “Whatever good things each person wants for himself, he should plan the same things for his neighbor as well.” Each of you would understand what is good in this way, if he were to reason with himself as follows: “You do not want to be murdered; do not murder another. You do not want your wife to be violated by another through adultery; do not commit adultery with another man’s wedded wife. You do not want any of your possessions to be stolen; do not steal anything belonging to another.” And so, recognizing from your own case what is reasonable and doing it, you will become dear to God and obtain healing; for otherwise you will be tormented in your bodies in the present age and punished in your souls in the age to come.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"ὑπὸ τοῦ προδρόμου Σίμωνος προαπατηθέντες","chosen":"after first being deceived by Simon the forerunner","rationale":"πρόδρομος explicitly calls Simon a forerunner, while προαπατάω presents the deception as prior; the translation does not specify whose forerunner he is."},{"source_quote":"διὰ τῆς μετανοίας","chosen":"through reorientation","rationale":"The context concerns moral and spiritual redirection expressed by accepting what pleases God. “Through repentance” is the traditional alternative."},{"source_quote":"καὶ τὰ σώματα ἀναρρῶσαι καὶ τὰς ψυχὰς ἀναλαβεῖν","chosen":"both restore your bodies to health and recover your souls","rationale":"ἀναρρωννύω denotes renewed bodily strength, while ἀναλαμβάνω here presents the souls as regained or recovered; “take up your souls again” would be more formally literal."},{"source_quote":"αὐτὸν αἰτεῖν ὡς πάντα νόμῳ κριτικῷ διδόντα","chosen":"to make requests of him as the one who gives everything according to a judicial law","rationale":"κριτικός can mean discriminating or judicial. “According to a law of discernment” is possible, but the surrounding emphasis on consequences and punishment favors “judicial.”"},{"source_quote":"νεκρᾶς μὴ γεύεσθαι σαρκός","chosen":"not to taste dead flesh","rationale":"The wording directly prohibits tasting flesh that is dead; it has not been generalized to a familiar dietary formula."},{"source_quote":"ἐν πολλοῖς σώμασιν μίαν γνώμην ἀναλαβόντες","chosen":"taking up one mind in many bodies","rationale":"The rendering retains the author’s image of bodily plurality united in a single judgment or disposition."},{"source_quote":"ἐπεὶ καὶ ἐν τῷ παρόντι αἰῶνι βασανισθήσεσθε","chosen":"for otherwise you will be tormented in your bodies in the present age","rationale":"After an exhortation or stated favorable outcome, ἐπεί can introduce the consequence that follows otherwise. The formally possible “since indeed you will be tormented” would obscure the warning contrast supplied by the context."}],"source_issues":[]},{"reference":"7.5","text":"After being instructed in such things by Peter over a few days and being healed, they were baptized. Then, all deeply grieved by his further wonders, they sat together as a whole populace in the middle of the marketplaces on ashes and sackcloth, reorienting themselves over the sins they had previously committed. When those in Sidon heard these things, they did the same and sent suppliants to Peter, since they themselves were unable to come to him because of their diseases. Peter, after staying in Tyre for not many days, instructing everyone in it, freeing them from every kind of affliction, forming a church, and appointing for them a bishop from among the elders who followed him, set out for Sidon. On learning that Peter was coming, Simon immediately fled to Beirut with Appion and his companions.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"τοιαῦτα ὑπὸ τοῦ Πέτρου ἐν ὀλίγαις ἡμέραις κατηχηθέντες","chosen":"After being instructed in such things by Peter over a few days","rationale":"κατηχέω here means to instruct orally; “catechized” would preserve the later technical term but would be less accessible in modern English."},{"source_quote":"τοῖς λοιποῖς αὐτοῦ θαύμασιν περίλυποι","chosen":"deeply grieved by his further wonders","rationale":"περίλυπος takes the dative as the cause or occasion of grief, and λοιπός can mean remaining, other, or further. “Deeply grieved at his other wonders” is a close alternative."},{"source_quote":"πανδημεὶ ἐπὶ σποδοῦ καὶ σάκκου ἐκαθέζοντο","chosen":"they sat together as a whole populace ... on ashes and sackcloth","rationale":"πανδημεί means collectively or with the whole populace, while ἐπί with the genitive presents ashes and sackcloth as what they sat upon."},{"source_quote":"μετανοοῦντες ἐπὶ τοῖς πρότερον ἡμαρτημένοις","chosen":"reorienting themselves over the sins they had previously committed","rationale":"The participle describes moral reorientation in response to earlier sins, while ἐπί identifies those sins as its occasion. “Repenting over their former sins” is the traditional alternative."},{"source_quote":"ἐκκλησίαν τε συστησάμενος","chosen":"forming a church","rationale":"In the context of appointing a bishop from among elders, ἐκκλησία denotes an organized congregation or church, and συνίστημι denotes forming or establishing it."},{"source_quote":"μαθὼν ἥκοντα τὸν Πέτρον","chosen":"On learning that Peter was coming","rationale":"In the narrative sequence Peter has just set out for Sidon, so the present participle is best understood as his approach. Because ἥκω can also have a perfect-like sense, “had arrived” remains grammatically possible."}],"source_issues":[]}]}
